items.text: A concept album whose lyrics draw on religion and divinity, the fourth record from a Danish progressive metal band.
items.why: Lead: 'the fourth studio album released by the Danish progressive metal band Royal Hunt. This is a concept album, with lyrics inspired by religion and divinity.'

items.text: Teichiku Records (Japan), Magna Carta Records (USA), Semaphore Records (Europe)
items.why: Infobox 'Label: Teichiku Records (Japan) Magna Carta Records (USA) Semaphore Records (Europe)'.

items.text: D. C. Cooper (vocals), André Andersen (keyboards and guitars), Steen Mogensen (bass guitar), Jacob Kjaer (guitar), Allan Sørensen (drums), with Maria McTurk, Lise Hansen and Kenny Lubcke on backing vocals
items.why: Personnel lists exactly these names and roles.

items.text: André Andersen wrote the songs, apart from the bonus track 'The Final Lullaby', which Steen Mogensen wrote.
items.why: Track listing: 'All songs written by André Andersen except where noted' and '"The Final Lullaby" [Bonus Track] – 4:01 (Steen Mogensen)'.

items.text: Lars H. Nissen and Royal Hunt handled the mix.
items.why: Production: 'Mixing – Lars H. Nissen and Royal Hunt'.

items.text: It is the only instrumental on the album.
items.why: Track listing: '"Martial Arts" (Instrumental)[Bonus Track] – 1:51'. The pack labels only this track instrumental but never says it is the only one (the 1:39 'The Awakening' carries no label either way), and it is a bonus track, not part of the main album. Title matches.

missed: Loudwire ranked it in 2025 as the 11th best progressive metal album of the 1990s (Lead). Beyond that the pack is thin; listen_for picked a 1:51 bonus track rather than anything from the main sequence such as the 9:31 'Time Will Tell'.
